newsitem.title: USA: Dade County, Fla., advances gasoline, fire taxes.
newsitem.headline: Dade County, Fla., advances gasoline, fire taxes.

text.p: Florida's Dade County Commission gave preliminary approval to proposals to raise the county's gasoline tax and its fire-rescue tax.
Both still must be approved in a second reading following public hearings.
The commission voted 6-4 Tuesday to raise the gasoline tax by one cent to 11 cents a gallon.

The commissoin cut that tax to 10 cents from 12 cents last year, but County Manager Armando Vidal said the partial restoration was needed to fund mass transit programs. The proposal would raise about $7.5 million a year, costing the average motorist about $6 annually.

Commissioners also voted 9-1 to require that property owners pay a special assessment for fire-rescue service. The assessment would be $17 for single-family homes but since the county plans to roll back the existing fire tax as part of the fiscal 1998 budget, the average increase would be about $10.
The proposals are part of the budget for the year that begins Oct 1, but must be approved ahead of the overall budget to meet state deadlines.
